'''Darryl Eugene''' "'''D. J.'''" '''Strawberry Jr.''' (born June 15, 1985) is an American-born naturalized Cameroonian<ref>[http://basketball.eurobasket.com/player/DJ-Strawberry/Turkey/Besiktas-Sompo-Japan-Istanbul/35521 D.J. STRAWBERRY basketball profile Nationality: USA-Cameroonian.]</ref> former professional [[basketball]] player. He is the son of former [[Major League Baseball]] player [[Darryl Strawberry]].

==High school career==
While living in [[Corona, California]], Strawberry attended [[Mater Dei High School (Santa Ana, California)|Mater Dei High School]] in [[Santa Ana, California|Santa Ana]].<ref name=UMD>{{cite web|url=http://www.umterps.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=29700&ATCLID=207383145|title=D.J. Strawberry|publisher=University of Maryland|access-date=June 25, 2018}}</ref> During Strawberry's senior year at Mater Dei, he defended future [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] superstar [[LeBron James]] in a nationally televised matchup against [[St. Vincent–St. Mary High School]] of [[Akron, Ohio]]. Strawberry was lauded for his efforts, which included holding James to a 33% shooting performance (8 for 24 from the field), and 0 for 8 from beyond the [[three-point field goal|three-point]] line).<ref>{{Cite web|title=ESPN.com: NBA - LeBron James good enough as top-ranked Irish roll|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/news/2003/0104/1487397.html|access-date=2021-01-23|website=www.espn.com}}</ref>

Considered a four-star recruit by [[247Sports]], Strawberry was listed as the No. 15 shooting guard and the No. 84 player in the nation in 2003.<ref>[https://247sports.com/Player/DJ-Strawberry-68218/?Institution=600 D. J. Strawberry Recruiting Profile]</ref>

==College career==
Strawberry assumed the role of a [[swingman]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland Terrapins]], and he was much valued for his on-the-ball defense. He averaged nearly 2 [[steal (basketball)|steals]] per game, leading his team in that category. He was also valued for his off-the-bench intensity; it is felt that Maryland's absence from the 2005 [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] was due in no small part to a season-ending [[Anterior cruciate ligament|ACL]] injury Strawberry suffered in mid-January of that year.

While he was primarily a swingman, a lack of depth pressed Strawberry into the role of [[point guard]] during his junior year. He had various degrees of success in this new role, leading the team in assists(4.0 per game). Strawberry received Honorable Mention All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] Freshman honors. During his junior year, he received Honorable Mention All-ACC Defensive Team honors, becoming the eighth player in Maryland history to lead the team in both steals and assists. In his senior season, Strawberry was voted to second team All-ACC.

==Professional career==
Strawberry was drafted by the [[Phoenix Suns]] with the 59th selection in the [[2007 NBA draft]]. He was signed on August 28, 2007, to a two-year contract.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/suns/news/strawberry_070828.html Suns sign D.J. Strawberry.]</ref>

===NBA D-League===
On December 18, 2007, it was announced he was assigned to the [[Canton Charge|Albuquerque Thunderbirds]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA D-League]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/suns/news/tucker_recalled.html Phoenix recalls D-League performer of the week Tucker.]</ref> He was named ''Performer of the Week'' for the week ending January 6. Strawberry was recalled to the Suns in place of another rookie, [[Alando Tucker]], on January 10, 2008.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20080115070155/http://www.nba.com/suns/news/dleague_08011.html Tucker heads to D-League, Strawberry is recalled.]</ref>

===2008–09 season===
On August 25, 2008, he was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] for [[Sean Singletary]],<ref>[https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3553531 Suns trade Strawberry to Rockets for rookie guard Singletary.]</ref> but was waived on October 24.<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=2074 Rockets waive DJ Strawberry ]</ref> Six days later, he signed with the Italian club [[Fortitudo Pallacanestro Bologna|Fortitudo Bologna]] for the rest of the season.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20081216115629/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/ulebcup/home/news/i/37122/448/item Fortitudo Bologna lands D.J. Strawberry.]</ref>

In April, 2009, he suffered a [[Meniscus (anatomy)|meniscus]] injury to his left knee, ending his season in Italy.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/76238/fortitudo-strawberry-to-undero-surgery.html Fortitudo, Strawberry to undero surgery]</ref> He then returned to the United States for surgery, and in July, 2009 he began a 6-month program in Los Angeles.

===2009–2022===
In January 2010, Strawberry joined the [[Stockton Kings|Reno Bighorns]] of the [[NBA G League|NBA D-League]].<ref>[http://www.rgj.com/article/20100130/SPORTS/100130010/1018/SPORTS Reno Bighorns announce they have acquired two new players]</ref>

In July 2010, Strawberry joined the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] for the 2010 [[NBA Summer League|NBA summer league]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/lakers/news/10summerleague.html Lakers 2010 Summer League Schedule and Roster | THE OFFICIAL SITE OF THE LOS ANGELES LAKERS]</ref> On September 17, 2010, he was signed by the [[New Orleans Pelicans|New Orleans Hornets]] to a non-guaranteed one-year deal.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/hornets_sign_dj_strwberry__2010_09_17.html HORNETS SIGN D.J. STRAWBERRY AND DARRYL WATKINS]</ref> However, he was later waived by the Hornets on October 20.<ref>[http://www.nola.com/hornets/index.ssf/2010/10/new_orleans_hornets_waive_guar.html New Orleans Hornets waive guard D.J. Strawberry, roster now stands at 15 ]</ref> Afterwards, Strawberry re-signed with the Reno Bighorns.<ref name="resignReno">{{cite web|title=Bighorns Re-Sign D.J. Strawberry|url=http://www.kolotv.com/sports/headlines/110735169.html|work=KOLOTV.com|access-date=28 November 2010|archive-date=17 July 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110717182236/http://www.kolotv.com/sports/headlines/110735169.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> On January 18, 2011, he signed with [[BC Rytas|Lietuvos rytas]] of Lithuania until the end of the 2010–11 season.<ref>[http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/81436/lietuvos-rytas-tops-backcourt-with-strawberry Lietuvos Rytas tops backcourt with Strawberry]</ref>

On August 26, 2011, Strawberry signed a two-year deal with the Israeli club [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/88236/hapoel-migdal-lands-dj-strawberry-for-two-years.html Hapoel Migdal lands DJ Strawberry for two years]</ref> After one season in which he averaged 15.6 points in the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League|Israeli League]], he parted ways with Hapoel on June 25, 2012.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/israel/92712/strawberry-randle-bradley-and-thomas-leave-hapoel-migdal-jerusalem.html Strawberry, Randle, Bradley and Thomas leave Hapoel Migdal Jerusalem]</ref>

On September 20, 2012, Strawberry signed with the Croatian club [[KK Cibona|Cibona]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Cibona officially pens a deal with DJ Strawberry|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/adriatic-league/95346/cibona-officially-pens-a-deal-with-dj-strawberry.html|work=Sportando|access-date=20 September 2012}}</ref> On June 22, 2013, Strawberry signed with the [[Capitanes de Arecibo]] of Puerto Rico for the 2013 [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|BSN]] season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Capitanes de Arecibo sign DJ Strawberry|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/102261/capitanes-de-arecibo-sign-dj-strawberry.html|work=Sportando|access-date=22 June 2013}}</ref> On July 12, 2013, he re-signed with Cibona.<ref>{{cite news|title=Cibona keep DJ Strawberry|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/adriatic-league/103553/cibona-keep-dj-strawberry.html|access-date=December 17, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=July 12, 2013}}</ref> On December 25, 2013, he was released by Cibona due to financial problems of the club.<ref>{{cite web|title=Cibona otpustila američki dvojac|url=http://crosarka.com/hrvatska-muska-kosarka/cibona/cibona-otpustila-americki-dvojac-96983|publisher=Crosarka.com|language=hr|access-date=26 December 2013|archive-date=29 December 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131229061149/http://crosarka.com/hrvatska-muska-kosarka/cibona/cibona-otpustila-americki-dvojac-96983|url-status=dead}}</ref> Two days later, he signed with [[Élan Béarnais Pau-Lacq-Orthez|Pau-Lacq-Orthez]] of France for the [[2013–14 Pro A season|rest of the season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Pau-Orthez announced DJ Strawberry|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/109738/pau-orthez-announced-dj-strawberry.html|access-date=30 December 2013|newspaper=Sportando.net|date=27 December 2013}}</ref>

On June 27, 2014, he signed with [[Piratas de Quebradillas]] of Puerto Rico for the 2014 BSN season.<ref>{{cite news|title=DJ Strawberry signs with Piratas de Quebradillas|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/124517/dj-strawberry-signs-with-piratas-de-quebradillas.html|access-date=June 27, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=June 27, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150702195529/http://www.sportando.com/en/world/america/124517/dj-strawberry-signs-with-piratas-de-quebradillas.html|archive-date=July 2, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref> On July 2, 2014, he signed a one-year deal with [[Karşıyaka Basket|Pınar Karşıyaka]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Turkish Basketball League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Pinar Karsiyaka lands DJ Strwarberry|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/125339/pinar-karsiyaka-lands-dj-strawberry.html|access-date=July 2, 2014|work=Sportando.com|date=July 2, 2014}}</ref>

On July 2, 2015, he signed a two-year contract with the Greek club and [[EuroLeague]] powerhouse [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Olympiacos adds Strawberry flavor to roster|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/66bcfhay6o4n6cb6|access-date=July 2, 2015|work=Euroleague.net|date=July 2, 2015}}</ref> After one season, he parted ways with Olympiacos.<ref>{{cite news|title=Strawberry won't continue in Olympiacos|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/featured/257827/strawberry-wont-continue-in-olympiacos|access-date=July 1, 2016|work=Eurohoops.net|date=June 6, 2016}}</ref>

On July 22, 2016, Strawberry signed with Turkish club [[Beşiktaş J.K. (men's basketball)|Beşiktaş]] for the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Besiktas announced D.J Strawberry|url=http://www.eurohoops.net/featured/285868/besiktas-announced-d-j-strawberry|access-date=July 22, 2016|work=Eurohoops.net|date=July 22, 2016}}</ref> On July 3, 2017, he re-signed with Beşiktaş for one more season.<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/239730/besiktas-re-signs-dj-strawberry.html Besiktas re-signs DJ Strawberry]</ref>

On July 29, 2018, Strawberry signed a one-year deal with [[CB Gran Canaria|Herbalife Gran Canaria]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Herbalife Gran Canaria tabs DJ Strawberry - Club Baloncesto Gran Canaria |url=https://cbgrancanaria.net/en/news/herbalife-gran-canaria-tabs-dj-strawberry/ |access-date=17 August 2018 |work=Club Baloncesto Gran Canaria |date=29 July 2018 |archive-date=17 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180817161253/https://cbgrancanaria.net/en/news/herbalife-gran-canaria-tabs-dj-strawberry/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On October 31, 2019, he signed with [[Orléans Loiret Basket]] of the [[LNB Pro A|French Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/orleans-ink-d-j-strawberry/|title=Orleans ink D.J. Strawberry|date=October 31, 2019|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=November 4, 2019}}</ref>

In June 2020, he signed for one term at [[Liga ACB]] team [[UCAM Murcia CB|UCAM Murcia]].<ref>{{cite news |title=DJ Strawberry es la primera pieza del nuevo proyecto del UCAM Murcia |url=https://www.marca.com/baloncesto/acb/2020/06/06/5edb781aca4741ec3f8b4590.html |work=[[Marca (newspaper)|Marca]] |date=6 June 2020 |language=es}}</ref> Strawberry parted ways with the team on June 30, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=DJ Strawberry, UCAM Murcia part ways |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/dj-strawberry-ucam-murcia-part-ways/ |website=Sportando |access-date=June 30, 2021 |date=June 30, 2021}}</ref>

He re-joined Orléans Loiret Basket on December 6, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=DJ Strawberry returns to Orleans |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/dj-strawberry-returns-to-orleans/ |website=Sportando |access-date=December 7, 2021 |date=December 6, 2021|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref>

On January 30, 2022, Strawberry signed with [[Zamalek SC (basketball)|Zamalek SC]] of the [[Egyptian Basketball Super League]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Zamalek SC signs DJ Strawberry |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/zamalek-sc-signs-dj-strawberry/ |website=Sportando |access-date=January 30, 2022 |date=January 30, 2022|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref> On February 12, he made his debut for the team when he recorded 5 points and 3 rebounds against [[San Pablo Burgos|Burgos]] in the [[2022 FIBA Intercontinental Cup]] semifinal.<ref>{{cite web |title=Zamalek v Hereda San Pablo Burgos boxscore - FIBA Intercontinental Cup 2022 - 11 February |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/intercontinentalcup/2022/game/1102/Zamalek-Hereda-San-Pablo-Burgos#tab=boxscore |website=FIBA.basketball |access-date=12 February 2022 |language=en}}</ref>

==Cameroon national team==
In 2017, Strawberry was cleared to play with the senior men's [[Cameroon men's national basketball team|Cameroon national basketball team]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/national-teams/national-teams/234591/dj-strawberry-can-play-for-cameroon-at-afrobasket.html DJ Strawberry can play for Cameroon at AfroBasket]</ref>
